name: Guessing the Greatest (hard version)
description: The only difference between the easy and the hard version is the limit to the number of queries . This is an interactive problem. There is an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ different numbers. In one query you can ask the position of the second maximum element in a subsegment $$$a[l..r]$$$. Find the position of the maximum element in the array in no more than 20 queries. A subsegment $$$a[l..r]$$$ is all the elements $$$a_l, a_{l + 1}, ..., a_r$$$. After asking this subsegment you will be given the position of the second maximum from this subsegment in the whole array.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ $$$(2 \leq n \leq 10^5)$$$ — the number of elements in the array.
approach_summary: Design an adaptive query strategy maintaining uncertainty bounds. Halve candidate space or probe tree centroids using at most the allowed query budget.
